issues.description: The template file src/de/tum/cit/ase/Farm.java does not provide the expected Farm class described in the problem statement and shown in the solution. Instead the template declares a class named AnimalFarm and contains duplicated/malformed code blocks (including an extra package declaration inside a method). This structural mismatch (filename Farm.java but wrong/invalid class content) conflicts with the UML and task text that expect a public class Farm with the listed attributes and methods, and will prevent students from compiling or implementing the intended Farm class.
issues.suggestedFix: Fix the template file src/de/tum/cit/ase/Farm.java so it declares public class Farm (matching the filename) in package de.tum.cit.ase and contains the expected attributes and method signatures (List<Animal> animals, addAnimal(Animal), feedAllAnimals(), singFarmSong(), getter/setter, and a no-arg constructor initializing the ArrayList). Remove the duplicated package declaration and malformed nested code blocks. Provide only the class skeleton (method bodies can be TODO) so students can implement according to the UML.

issues.description: The template repository defines the main farm class as 'AnimalFarm' (in src/de/tum/cit/ase/Farm.java), while both the problem statement and the solution use the class name 'Farm'. This mismatch (file named Farm.java but class named AnimalFarm) breaks the direct mapping between the exercise description/UML and the provided starter code, likely confusing students who are instructed to implement or use a 'Farm' class and see references to 'Farm' in Main.java and the problem text.
issues.suggestedFix: Rename the class in src/de/tum/cit/ase/Farm.java from 'AnimalFarm' to 'Farm' (or otherwise make the template class name match the problem statement/UML and the solution). Ensure the public class name matches the file name and that Main.java and the exercise instructions consistently reference 'Farm'.
